questions.explanation: The Indian landmass was part of Gondwana. It later separated and moved northward as the intervening oceanic lithosphere was consumed at convergent margins. The Neo-Tethys oceanic lithosphere between India and Eurasia was progressively consumed by subduction. Eventually, continental collision occurred, and continued convergence caused underthrusting, folding, thrusting and crustal thickening.
questions.source: Plate Tectonics PDF, Sections 12, 14 and 20 (Short-answer practice)

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Describe the stages in the formation of the Himalayas. Which of the following is the correct order?

options.A: Gondwana → northward movement → Neo-Tethys subduction → continental collision → crustal thickening → Himalayas and Tibetan Plateau
options.B: Continental collision → Gondwana → northward movement → Neo-Tethys subduction → Himalayas
options.C: Neo-Tethys subduction → Gondwana → continental collision → northward movement → Himalayas
options.D: Himalayas → continental collision → Neo-Tethys subduction → northward movement → Gondwana

questions.explanation: The study strategy states: First memorise the three plate-boundary types and their landforms. Then learn the Indian Plate-Eurasian Plate sequence: Gondwana → northward movement → Neo-Tethys subduction → continental collision → crustal thickening → Himalayas and Tibetan Plateau.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Differentiate a mid-ocean ridge from an ocean trench. Which of the following correctly contrasts them?

options.A: Mid-ocean ridge: divergent boundary, new oceanic lithosphere forms, elevated submarine mountain chain, basaltic volcanism and shallow earthquakes; Ocean trench: convergent/subduction boundary, oceanic lithosphere descends and is recycled, deep narrow ocean-floor depression, earthquakes from shallow to deep and often a volcanic arc nearby
options.B: Mid-ocean ridge: convergent boundary, deep depression; Ocean trench: divergent boundary, elevated mountain chain
options.C: Mid-ocean ridge: transform boundary; Ocean trench: divergent boundary
options.D: Mid-ocean ridge: subduction zone; Ocean trench: spreading centre

questions.explanation: A mid-ocean ridge is associated with divergent boundaries where new oceanic lithosphere forms; it is an elevated submarine mountain chain with basaltic volcanism, hydrothermal activity and shallow earthquakes. An ocean trench is associated with convergent/subduction boundaries where oceanic lithosphere descends and is recycled; it is a deep, narrow ocean-floor depression with earthquakes from shallow to deep and often a volcanic arc nearby.
questions.source: Plate Tectonics PDF, Section 10 (Table) and Section 20 (Short-answer practice)

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which NCERT book covers the interior of the Earth, distribution of oceans and continents, and plate tectonics?

options.A: NCERT, Fundamentals of Physical Geography
options.B: NCERT, India: Physical Environment

questions.explanation: NCERT, Fundamentals of Physical Geography covers the interior of the Earth, distribution of oceans and continents, and plate tectonics.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which NCERT book covers the structure and physiography of India, Himalayan region and tectonic setting?

options.A: NCERT, Fundamentals of Physical Geography
options.B: NCERT, India: Physical Environment

questions.explanation: NCERT, India: Physical Environment covers the structure and physiography of India, Himalayan region and tectonic setting.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which organisation provides educational resources on plate tectonics, subduction, earthquakes, volcanoes and seafloor spreading?

options.A: ISRO
options.B: US Geological Survey (USGS)

questions.explanation: US Geological Survey (USGS) provides plate tectonics, subduction, earthquakes, volcanoes and seafloor spreading educational resources.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which organisation provides resources on ocean ridges, trenches and seafloor features?

options.A: NOAA Ocean Exploration
options.B: Geological Survey of India

questions.explanation: NOAA Ocean Exploration provides resources on ocean ridges, trenches and seafloor features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which organisation provides Indian geology, Himalayan tectonics and geological maps?

options.A: NOAA
options.B: Geological Survey of India (GSI)

questions.explanation: Geological Survey of India (GSI) provides Indian geology, Himalayan tectonics and geological maps.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the general crustal effect at divergent boundaries?

options.A: Lithosphere may be consumed at subduction zones
options.B: New lithosphere commonly forms

questions.explanation: At divergent boundaries, new lithosphere commonly forms.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the general crustal effect at convergent boundaries?

options.A: New lithosphere commonly forms
options.B: Lithosphere may be consumed at subduction zones; collision thickens crust

questions.explanation: At convergent boundaries, lithosphere may be consumed at subduction zones; collision thickens crust.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the general crustal effect at transform boundaries?

options.A: New lithosphere commonly forms
options.B: Lithosphere may be consumed at subduction zones
options.C: Generally neither creates nor destroys lithosphere

questions.explanation: At transform boundaries, generally neither creates nor destroys lithosphere.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical feature of divergent boundaries?

options.A: Trenches, volcanic arcs and fold mountains
options.B: Rifts, mid-ocean ridges, shallow earthquakes and basaltic volcanism

questions.explanation: Typical features of divergent boundaries include rifts, mid-ocean ridges, shallow earthquakes and basaltic volcanism.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical feature of convergent boundaries?

options.A: Rifts and mid-ocean ridges
options.B: Trenches, volcanic arcs, fold mountains and earthquakes

questions.explanation: Typical features of convergent boundaries include trenches, volcanic arcs, fold mountains and earthquakes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical feature of transform boundaries?

options.A: Rifts and mid-ocean ridges
options.B: Trenches and volcanic arcs

questions.explanation: Typical features of transform boundaries include strike-slip faults and earthquakes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the maximum depth of earthquakes in some subduction systems according to the Wadati-Benioff zone?

options.A: About 70 km
options.B: About 300 km

questions.explanation: Earthquakes can occur from shallow depths to several hundred kilometres, reaching about 700 km in some subduction systems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the commonly cited depth of Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench?

options.A: Around 5.9 kilometres
options.B: Around 8.9 kilometres

questions.explanation: Published depth estimates vary with measurement method and survey; commonly cited values are around 10.9 kilometres.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a commonly cited geodetic estimate of the Indian Plate's motion relative to Eurasia?

options.A: Around 0.4-0.5 cm per year
options.B: Around 4-5 cm per year

questions.explanation: Present-day motion is on the order of a few centimetres per year, with commonly cited geodetic estimates around 4-5 cm per year relative to Eurasia in parts of the region.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a major tectonic boundary in the Himalayan region?

options.A: The San Andreas Fault
options.B: The Main Himalayan Thrust system

questions.explanation: The Himalayan region contains major tectonic boundaries such as the Indus-Yarlung Tsangpo Suture Zone and the Main Himalayan Thrust system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a major geological suture marking the former boundary between the Indian and Eurasian continental systems?

options.A: The San Andreas Fault
options.B: The Indus-Yarlung Tsangpo Suture Zone

questions.explanation: The Indus-Yarlung Tsangpo Suture Zone is a major geological suture marking the former boundary between the Indian and Eurasian continental systems and preserving evidence of the intervening Neo-Tethys oceanic realm.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of mid-ocean ridges?

options.A: Elevated ridge crests
options.B: Central rift valleys in some slower-spreading sections
options.C: High heat flow and basaltic volcanism

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges have elevated ridge crests, central rift valleys in some slower-spreading sections, high heat flow, basaltic volcanism, hydrothermal activity and shallow earthquakes. Deep, narrow ocean-floor depressions are characteristic of ocean trenches, not mid-ocean ridges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What drives decompression melting at mid-ocean ridges?

options.A: Increase in pressure as mantle rises
options.B: Decrease in pressure as hot mantle rises beneath the gap between diverging plates
options.C: Addition of water from the ocean

questions.explanation: Hot mantle rises beneath the gap between diverging plates; pressure decreases and partial melting produces magma.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between mantle convection and plate motion?

options.A: Mantle convection is the sole driver of plate motion
options.B: Mantle convection plays no role in plate motion
options.C: Heat-driven mantle circulation contributes to the dynamic environment in which plates move; mantle flow and plate motion interact
options.D: Mantle convection only occurs at transform boundaries

questions.explanation: Heat-driven mantle circulation contributes to the dynamic environment in which plates move. Mantle flow and plate motion interact; simple textbook diagrams of convection cells are useful models but do not capture every detail of real mantle dynamics.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the forces contributing to plate motion?

options.A: A single universal mechanism explains all plate motion
options.B: Plate motion reflects a combination of forces and resistance, rather than one universal mechanism
options.C: Only slab pull drives plate motion
options.D: Only ridge push drives plate motion

questions.explanation: Plate motion reflects a combination of forces and resistance, rather than one universal mechanism. Important forces include slab pull, ridge push and tractions associated with mantle flow.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Indian Plate's boundaries?

options.A: They are simple and straight on all sides
options.B: They are complex, involving collision, underthrusting, subduction and spreading systems

questions.explanation: The boundaries of the Indian Plate are complex. The northern margin is associated with collision and underthrusting beneath Eurasia along the Himalayan region; the western and northwestern margins interact with the Arabian and Eurasian plate systems; the eastern margin is part of a complex subduction and collision zone around the Indo-Burma region; and the southern and southeastern oceanic boundaries include spreading systems in the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the India-Asia collision?

options.A: It was an instantaneous event
options.B: It was a prolonged, spatially complex process; the exact timing of initial contact and subsequent stages is an active research subject
options.C: It occurred exactly 50 million years ago with no uncertainty

questions.explanation: The India-Asia collision was a prolonged, spatially complex process. The exact timing of initial contact and subsequent stages is an active research subject; school-level accounts commonly place the main collision in the early Cenozoic, around 50 million years ago, but estimates vary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rivers drains large parts of the Himalayas and adjacent regions?

options.A: The Amazon
options.B: The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra

questions.explanation: The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems drain large parts of the Himalayas and adjacent regions. Their headwaters, tributaries and valleys are strongly influenced by mountain uplift, glaciation and erosion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the formation of the Himalayas?

options.A: They formed through a simple oceanic-continental volcanic-arc process
options.B: They formed mainly through continental collision between the Indian and Eurasian plates

questions.explanation: The Himalayas formed mainly through continental collision, not through a simple oceanic-continental volcanic-arc process.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the melting process above subduction zones?

options.A: The entire descending slab melts immediately
options.B: Water and other volatiles released from the descending slab promote melting in the mantle wedge above it
options.C: Melting occurs due to friction between the plates
options.D: Melting occurs due to tidal heating

questions.explanation: Water and other volatiles released from the descending slab promote melting in the mantle wedge above it. Magma can rise through the overriding plate and form a volcanic arc. The process is not simply because the entire slab melts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which boundary type is associated with the formation of new oceanic crust?

options.A: Divergent boundaries
options.B: Convergent boundaries

questions.explanation: At divergent boundaries, new oceanic crust commonly forms at spreading ridges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which boundary type is associated with the consumption or recycling of oceanic lithosphere?

options.A: Divergent boundaries
options.B: Convergent boundaries

questions.explanation: At convergent boundaries, oceanic lithosphere may be consumed at subduction zones.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the classification of major and minor plates?

options.A: The classification is fixed and identical in all textbooks
options.B: Classification as major or minor can vary among maps and textbooks
options.D: All plates are the same size

questions.explanation: Classification as major or minor can vary among maps and textbooks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a minor plate with its location or significance?

options.A: Nazca Plate - off western South America; subducts beneath the South American Plate
options.B: Nazca Plate - off Central America; subducts beneath the Caribbean Plate
options.C: Nazca Plate - in the western Pacific; involved in island-arc systems
options.D: Nazca Plate - between South America and Antarctica

questions.explanation: The Nazca Plate is located off western South America; it subducts beneath the South American Plate and contributes to the Andes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a minor plate with its location or significance?

options.A: Cocos Plate - off western South America; subducts beneath the South American Plate
options.B: Cocos Plate - off Central America; subducts beneath parts of the Caribbean and North American plate systems
options.C: Cocos Plate - in the western Pacific; involved in island-arc systems
options.D: Cocos Plate - between South America and Antarctica

questions.explanation: The Cocos Plate is located off Central America; it subducts beneath parts of the Caribbean and North American plate systems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a minor plate with its location or significance?

options.A: Arabian Plate - in the Arabian Peninsula; moves generally northward towards Eurasia
options.B: Arabian Plate - off western South America; subducts beneath the South American Plate
options.C: Arabian Plate - in the western Pacific; involved in island-arc systems
options.D: Arabian Plate - between South America and Antarctica

questions.explanation: The Arabian Plate is located in the Arabian Peninsula; it moves generally northward towards Eurasia.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a minor plate with its location or significance?

options.A: Somali Plate - off western South America; subducts beneath the South American Plate
options.B: Somali Plate - in the eastern part of Africa, separating from the Nubian part of the African Plate in the East African Rift system
options.C: Somali Plate - in the western Pacific; involved in island-arc systems
options.D: Somali Plate - between South America and Antarctica

questions.explanation: The Somali Plate is located in the eastern part of Africa, separating from the Nubian part of the African Plate in the East African Rift system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relative movement at a divergent boundary?

options.A: Plates move towards each other
options.B: Plates move apart
options.C: Plates slide laterally past each other

questions.explanation: At a divergent boundary, plates move apart.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relative movement at a convergent boundary?

options.A: Plates move apart
options.B: Plates move towards each other
options.C: Plates slide laterally past each other

questions.explanation: At a convergent boundary, plates move towards each other.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relative movement at a transform boundary?

options.A: Plates move apart
options.B: Plates move towards each other
options.C: Plates slide laterally past each other

questions.explanation: At a transform boundary, plates slide laterally past each other.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main feature of a subduction zone?

options.A: A deep-sea trench
options.B: A dipping zone of earthquakes called the Wadati-Benioff zone
options.C: A volcanic arc on the overriding plate
options.D: A mid-ocean ridge with a central rift valley

questions.explanation: Main features of a subduction zone include a deep-sea trench, a dipping zone of earthquakes called the Wadati-Benioff zone, deformation and accretion of sediments, possible forearc and back-arc regions, and commonly a volcanic arc on the overriding plate. A mid-ocean ridge with a central rift valley is characteristic of divergent boundaries, not subduction zones.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the age of oceanic crust relative to mid-ocean ridges?

options.A: Oceanic crust is oldest near the ridge axis
options.B: Oceanic crust is youngest near the ridge axis and older farther away
options.C: Oceanic crust age is uniform everywhere
options.D: Oceanic crust age is unrelated to distance from ridges

questions.explanation: New crust is formed at the ridge axis and moves away as additional magma solidifies. Therefore, the youngest oceanic crust is generally near the ridge, while older crust occurs farther away.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the balance of lithosphere creation and destruction?

options.A: New oceanic lithosphere formed at ridges is balanced over geological time by destruction or recycling at subduction zones
options.B: The Earth is continuously expanding because of seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: New oceanic lithosphere formed at ridges is balanced over geological time by the destruction or recycling of oceanic lithosphere at subduction zones, so the process does not imply continuous expansion of Earth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Mid-Atlantic Ridge?

options.A: It separates the North American and Eurasian plates in the north and the South American and African plates in the south
options.B: It is a convergent boundary
options.C: It is located in the Pacific Ocean

questions.explanation: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is the divergent plate boundary running through the Atlantic Ocean, separating the North American and Eurasian plates in the north and the South American and African plates in the south.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the shape of ocean trenches?

options.A: They are commonly arcuate or curved in plan
options.B: They are perfectly straight

questions.explanation: Ocean trenches are commonly arcuate or curved in plan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the formation of fold mountains?

options.A: They form mainly through compression that bends and shortens rock layers
options.B: They form mainly through extension
options.C: They form mainly through volcanic accumulation
options.D: They form mainly through transform faulting

questions.explanation: Fold mountains form mainly through compression that bends and shortens rock layers. Large fold-and-thrust belts commonly develop at convergent margins. The Himalayas are a major example.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about fault-block mountains?

options.A: They form when crustal blocks are uplifted, tilted or relatively elevated along faults, commonly under extensional tectonic conditions
options.B: They form mainly through compression and folding
options.C: They form mainly through volcanic accumulation

questions.explanation: Fault-block mountains form when crustal blocks are uplifted, tilted or relatively elevated along faults, commonly under extensional tectonic conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about crustal thickening?

options.A: It occurs when compression shortens and stacks crustal rocks through folding, thrust faulting and underthrusting
options.B: It occurs when the crust thins due to extension
options.C: It occurs only at divergent boundaries
options.D: It occurs only at transform boundaries

questions.explanation: Crustal thickening occurs when compression shortens and stacks crustal rocks through folding, thrust faulting and underthrusting. The thicker crust can develop high elevations through isostatic adjustment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Indian Plate's motion?

options.A: It has moved southward from Laurasia
options.B: It moved northward and later north-northeastward towards Eurasia; the exact direction and rate have varied through geological time
options.D: It moved eastward towards the Pacific

questions.explanation: In broad terms, the Indian Plate moved northward and later north-northeastward towards Eurasia. The exact direction and rate have varied through geological time.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the consumption of the Neo-Tethys Ocean?

options.A: Its oceanic lithosphere was progressively consumed by subduction during convergence between India and Eurasia
options.B: It was consumed by seafloor spreading
options.C: It was consumed by transform faulting
options.D: It still exists today between India and Eurasia

questions.explanation: The Neo-Tethys Ocean was the oceanic basin that separated the Indian/Gondwanan margin from Eurasia before the India-Asia collision. Its oceanic lithosphere was progressively consumed during convergence.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Indian continental crust during collision?

options.A: It is relatively buoyant and resists deep subduction
options.B: It is denser than oceanic crust and subducts deeply
options.D: It is the same density as the asthenosphere

questions.explanation: Continental crust is relatively buoyant and resists deep subduction. When the Indian continental margin reached the Eurasian margin after oceanic lithosphere had been consumed, the collision produced shortening, underthrusting and crustal thickening rather than simple continued oceanic-style subduction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the elevation changes in the Himalayas?

options.A: Tectonic uplift continues, but actual surface elevation changes vary because uplift is balanced locally by erosion, landslides, river incision and other processes
options.B: The Himalayas are rising at a constant rate everywhere
options.C: The Himalayas are not rising at all

questions.explanation: Tectonic uplift continues in parts of the Himalayan region, but actual surface elevation changes vary because uplift is balanced locally by erosion, landslides, river incision and other processes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Tibetan Plateau?

options.A: It is one of the world's highest and largest plateaus, formed by collision and continuing convergence that thickened and elevated the crust north of the Himalayas
options.B: It is a volcanic plateau formed by hotspot activity

questions.explanation: The collision and continuing convergence thickened and elevated the crust north of the Himalayas, contributing to the formation of the Tibetan Plateau, one of the world's highest and largest plateaus.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Himalayan region's vulnerability to landslides?

options.A: Active tectonics create steep, fractured and uplifted terrain; heavy monsoon rainfall, river erosion, weathering, slope cutting and earthquakes can destabilise slopes and trigger landslides
options.B: Landslides occur only due to volcanic eruptions
options.C: Landslides do not occur in the Himalayan region
options.D: Landslides occur only due to seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: Active tectonics create steep, fractured and uplifted terrain. Heavy monsoon rainfall, river erosion, weathering, slope cutting and earthquakes can destabilise slopes and trigger landslides.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between plate boundaries and earthquakes?

options.A: Most plate-related earthquakes occur at plate boundaries
options.B: Earthquakes only occur in plate interiors
options.C: Earthquakes do not occur at plate boundaries
options.D: Earthquakes occur only at transform boundaries

questions.explanation: Plate boundaries are zones where most plate-related earthquakes, volcanoes and major deformation occur.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the development of plate tectonics?

options.A: It emerged from the combined work of many scientists
options.B: It was developed by a single scientist
options.C: It was developed in the 19th century
options.D: It was developed before continental drift

questions.explanation: Plate tectonics emerged from the combined work of many scientists, including Alfred Wegener, Arthur Holmes, Harry Hess, Robert Dietz, and Vine, Matthews and Morley.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the mechanism of continental drift as proposed by Wegener?

options.A: Wegener provided an adequate mechanism for continental motion
options.B: Wegener argued that continents move but did not provide an adequate mechanism
options.C: Wegener argued that continents are fixed

questions.explanation: Continental drift, proposed by Alfred Wegener, argued that continents move but did not provide an adequate mechanism. Plate tectonics later explained that entire lithospheric plates move.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the asthenosphere's physical state?

options.A: It is a global ocean of liquid magma
options.B: It is predominantly solid rock that can deform and flow slowly over geological time
options.C: It is the same as the outer core
options.D: It is the rigid outer shell

questions.explanation: The asthenosphere is predominantly solid rock that can deform and flow slowly over geological time; it is not a global ocean of liquid magma.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the deeper mantle in the context of plate tectonics?

options.A: It is solid rock that convects over geological time
options.B: It is completely liquid
options.D: It is the same as the crust

questions.explanation: The deeper mantle is solid rock that convects over geological time and is part of the thermal and dynamic system influencing plate motion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the speed of plate motion on a human timescale?

options.A: Motion is slow on a human timescale but large over millions of years
options.B: Motion is fast on a human timescale
options.D: Motion is only measurable during earthquakes

questions.explanation: Most plates move at rates of a few millimetres to several centimetres per year. Motion is slow on a human timescale but large over millions of years.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Pacific Plate's boundaries?

options.A: It is surrounded by many active plate boundaries, including subduction zones that contribute to the Ring of Fire
options.B: It has no active boundaries
options.C: It is surrounded only by divergent boundaries
options.D: It is surrounded only by transform boundaries

questions.explanation: The Pacific Plate is the largest plate and is surrounded by many active plate boundaries, including subduction zones that contribute to the circum-Pacific earthquake and volcanic belt known as the Ring of Fire.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between subduction and mountain building?

options.A: Subduction contributes to trenches, earthquakes, volcanic arcs, mountain belts, metamorphism and recycling of crustal materials into the mantle
options.B: Subduction only creates new oceanic crust
options.C: Subduction does not contribute to mountain building
options.D: Subduction only occurs at transform boundaries

questions.explanation: Subduction consumes oceanic lithosphere and contributes to trenches, earthquakes, volcanic arcs, mountain belts, metamorphism and recycling of crustal materials into the mantle.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between magnetic stripes and seafloor spreading?

options.A: The roughly symmetrical pattern of magnetic stripes on either side of a ridge supports the formation of new crust and its movement away from the ridge
options.B: Magnetic stripes are random and provide no evidence
options.C: Magnetic stripes occur only on continents
options.D: Magnetic stripes are caused by ocean currents

questions.explanation: Magnetic stripes are bands of oceanic crust recording alternating normal and reversed geomagnetic polarity as basalt cooled and acquired a magnetic signature. Their roughly symmetrical pattern on either side of a ridge supports the formation of new crust and its movement away from the ridge.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between Iceland and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge?

options.A: Iceland lies on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and is also influenced by a mantle plume or hotspot
options.B: Iceland is located on a transform boundary
options.C: Iceland is located on a subduction zone
options.D: Iceland is far from the Mid-Atlantic Ridge

questions.explanation: Iceland lies on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and is also influenced by a mantle plume or hotspot. Its position makes it an accessible example of an active divergent plate-boundary environment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between trenches and subduction?

options.A: The trench marks the surface expression of the bending and initial descent of the subducting plate
options.B: The trench is formed by seafloor spreading
options.C: The trench is formed by transform motion
options.D: The trench is unrelated to subduction

questions.explanation: The trench marks the surface expression of the bending and initial descent of the subducting plate. The slab then descends beneath the overriding plate, generating a dipping zone of earthquakes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between mountain building and erosion?

options.A: Mountain building involves tectonic uplift and crustal thickening, while erosion simultaneously modifies mountain relief
options.B: Erosion does not affect mountain relief
options.C: Mountain building occurs only through erosion
options.D: Erosion only occurs after mountain building stops

questions.explanation: Mountain building involves tectonic uplift and crustal thickening, while erosion simultaneously modifies mountain relief.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Indian Plate's relationship to Gondwana?

options.A: The Indian landmass was part of the southern supercontinent Gondwana
options.B: The Indian landmass was part of Laurasia
options.C: The Indian landmass was never part of any supercontinent
options.D: The Indian landmass was part of the Pacific Plate

questions.explanation: The Indian landmass was part of the southern supercontinent Gondwana. It later separated and moved northward as the intervening oceanic lithosphere was consumed at convergent margins.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Eurasian Plate's southern boundary?

options.A: It is tectonically complex, involving collision and subduction systems from the Mediterranean region through the Middle East and Himalayas to Southeast Asia
options.B: It is a simple divergent boundary
options.C: It is a simple transform boundary

questions.explanation: The Eurasian Plate's southern boundary is tectonically complex, involving collision and subduction systems from the Mediterranean region through the Middle East and Himalayas to Southeast Asia.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the geological structures formed by the India-Eurasia collision?

options.A: A major fold-and-thrust belt, the Himalayan mountain chain, the Tibetan Plateau, large fault systems and zones of intense seismicity formed
options.B: Only a mid-ocean ridge formed

questions.explanation: A major fold-and-thrust belt, the Himalayan mountain chain, the Tibetan Plateau, large fault systems and zones of intense seismicity formed due to the collision. The collision also caused widespread metamorphism and magmatism in parts of the broader region.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau?

options.A: The collision and continuing convergence thickened and elevated the crust north of the Himalayas, contributing to the formation of the Tibetan Plateau
options.B: The Tibetan Plateau is unrelated to the Himalayan collision
options.C: The Tibetan Plateau formed before the Himalayas
options.D: The Tibetan Plateau is a mid-ocean ridge

questions.explanation: The collision and continuing convergence thickened and elevated the crust north of the Himalayas, contributing to the formation of the Tibetan Plateau, one of the world's highest and largest plateaus.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Vine-Matthews-Morley hypothesis?

options.A: It explained magnetic stripes as evidence of spreading
options.B: It explained continental drift
options.C: It explained the formation of the Himalayas

questions.explanation: The Vine-Matthews-Morley hypothesis explained magnetic stripes as evidence of spreading.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about Robert Dietz's contribution to plate tectonics?

options.A: He contributed to the development of the seafloor-spreading hypothesis
options.B: He proposed continental drift
options.D: He proposed the theory of transform faults

questions.explanation: Robert Dietz also contributed to the development of the seafloor-spreading hypothesis.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the rigid uppermost mantle's role in plate tectonics?

options.A: It is attached mechanically to the crust and together with the crust forms the lithosphere
options.B: It is part of the asthenosphere
options.C: It is the same as the outer core
options.D: It is liquid and does not move

questions.explanation: The rigid uppermost mantle is strong upper mantle attached mechanically to the crust. Together with the crust, it forms the lithosphere.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the East African Rift?

options.A: It is an important continental rift system associated with divergent boundaries
options.B: It is a mid-ocean ridge

questions.explanation: The East African Rift is an important continental rift system associated with divergent boundaries.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the western Pacific's tectonic setting?

options.A: It contains several examples of complex island-arc and subduction systems
options.B: It contains only divergent boundaries

questions.explanation: The western Pacific contains several examples of complex island-arc and subduction systems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the San Andreas Fault system?

options.A: It is a transform boundary between the Pacific and North American plate systems
options.B: It is a mid-ocean ridge

questions.explanation: The San Andreas Fault system in California is a well-known example of a transform boundary between the Pacific and North American plate systems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the forearc and back-arc regions in subduction zones?

options.A: They are possible features of subduction zones, along with deformation and accretion of sediments
options.B: They are features of mid-ocean ridges
options.C: They are features of transform boundaries
options.D: They do not exist in subduction zones

questions.explanation: Main features of a subduction zone include a deep-sea trench, a dipping zone of earthquakes called the Wadati-Benioff zone, deformation and accretion of sediments, possible forearc and back-arc regions, and commonly a volcanic arc on the overriding plate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the distribution of ocean-floor sediments as evidence for seafloor spreading?

options.A: The distribution of ocean-floor sediments is evidence supporting seafloor spreading
options.B: Sediment distribution is uniform everywhere and provides no evidence
options.C: Sediments are found only on continents
options.D: Sediments are unrelated to seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: Evidence supporting seafloor spreading includes symmetrical magnetic anomaly stripes, the general increase in oceanic crust age away from ridges, high heat flow near ridge crests, and the distribution of ocean-floor sediments.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about hydrothermal activity at mid-ocean ridges?

options.A: Hydrothermal activity is a characteristic of mid-ocean ridges
options.B: Hydrothermal activity occurs only at transform boundaries
options.C: Hydrothermal activity occurs only at ocean trenches
options.D: Hydrothermal activity does not occur at mid-ocean ridges

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges have elevated ridge crests, central rift valleys in some slower-spreading sections, high heat flow, basaltic volcanism, hydrothermal activity and shallow earthquakes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the relationship between ocean trenches and volcanic arcs?

options.A: Ocean trenches are associated with subduction and often have volcanic arcs nearby
options.B: Ocean trenches are associated with divergent boundaries and have no volcanic arcs
options.C: Ocean trenches are associated with transform boundaries and have no volcanic arcs
options.D: Ocean trenches are unrelated to volcanic arcs

questions.explanation: Ocean trenches are associated with subduction, powerful earthquakes and volcanic arcs in many regions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the formation of volcanic mountains?

options.A: Many form above subduction zones; others occur at hotspots or divergent settings
options.B: They form only at transform boundaries
options.C: They form only through continental collision

questions.explanation: Volcanic mountains form when erupted lava, ash and other volcanic material accumulate around a vent or along a volcanic system. Many form above subduction zones; others occur at hotspots or divergent settings.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Indian Plate's northern margin?

options.A: It is associated with collision and underthrusting beneath Eurasia along the Himalayan region
options.B: It is a simple divergent boundary
options.C: It is a simple transform boundary

questions.explanation: The northern margin of the Indian Plate is associated with collision and underthrusting beneath Eurasia along the Himalayan region.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Indian Plate's eastern margin?

options.A: It is part of a complex subduction and collision zone around the Indo-Burma region
options.B: It is a simple divergent boundary
options.C: It is a simple transform boundary

questions.explanation: The eastern margin of the Indian Plate is part of a complex subduction and collision zone around the Indo-Burma region.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Indian Plate's southern and southeastern oceanic boundaries?

options.A: They include spreading systems in the Indian Ocean
options.B: They are simple transform boundaries

questions.explanation: The southern and southeastern oceanic boundaries of the Indian Plate include spreading systems in the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the timing of the India-Asia collision?

options.A: School-level accounts commonly place the main collision in the early Cenozoic, around 50 million years ago, but estimates vary
options.B: The collision occurred exactly 500 million years ago with no uncertainty

questions.explanation: The exact timing of initial contact and subsequent stages is an active research subject; school-level accounts commonly place the main collision in the early Cenozoic, around 50 million years ago, but estimates vary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Himalayas as 'young fold mountains'?

options.A: They are geologically young compared with ancient mountain systems and were formed largely by folding, thrusting and crustal thickening
options.B: They are the oldest mountains on Earth
options.C: They are made of young volcanic rocks
options.D: They formed in the last 1000 years

questions.explanation: They are geologically young compared with ancient mountain systems and were formed largely by folding, thrusting and crustal thickening during the ongoing India-Eurasia collision.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Trans-Himalaya, Greater Himalaya, Lesser Himalaya and Sub-Himalaya (Sivalik) belt?

options.A: They are a simplified north-south structural division of the Himalayas
options.B: They are mid-ocean ridges
options.D: They are continental rifts in Africa

questions.explanation: A simplified north-south structural division includes the Trans-Himalaya, Greater or Higher Himalaya, Lesser Himalaya and Sub-Himalaya (Sivalik) belt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In the summary comparison of the India-Eurasia collision, which stage resulted in the Himalayan mountain belt and Tibetan Plateau uplift?

options.A: The Gondwana stage
options.B: The northward movement stage

questions.explanation: During the orogeny stage, folding, thrusting and crustal thickening led to Himalayan mountain belt and Tibetan Plateau uplift.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In the summary comparison of the India-Eurasia collision, which stage involved the Indian continental margin reaching Eurasia?

options.A: The Gondwana stage
options.B: The continental collision stage

questions.explanation: During the continental collision stage, the Indian continental margin reached Eurasia, causing compression, underthrusting and crustal shortening.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In the summary comparison of the India-Eurasia collision, which stage involved Neo-Tethys oceanic lithosphere descending beneath the Eurasian margin?

options.A: The Gondwana stage
options.B: The northward movement stage

questions.explanation: During the subduction stage, Neo-Tethys oceanic lithosphere descended beneath the Eurasian margin in stages; the ocean basin narrowed and was consumed.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In the summary comparison of the India-Eurasia collision, which stage involved India moving towards Eurasia with oceanic lithosphere between them?

options.A: The Gondwana stage
options.B: The northward movement stage

questions.explanation: During the northward movement stage, India moved towards Eurasia; oceanic lithosphere lay between them, resulting in progressive closure of Neo-Tethys.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In the summary comparison of the India-Eurasia collision, which stage involved India being connected to southern continental fragments?

options.A: The Gondwana stage
options.B: The northward movement stage

questions.explanation: In the Gondwana stage, the Indian landmass was connected to southern continental fragments, and India was part of Gondwana.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a common exam trap regarding the number of major plates?

options.A: Some textbooks list seven major plates and combine India and Australia; modern maps may separate the Indian and Australian plates
options.B: All textbooks list exactly seven major plates with no variation
options.C: There is only one major plate

questions.explanation: Some textbooks list seven major plates and combine India and Australia; modern maps may separate the Indian and Australian plates. This is a common exam trap.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a common exam trap regarding the relationship between mid-ocean ridges and trenches?

options.A: Mid-ocean ridges are elevated submarine spreading centres, not trenches; ocean trenches are associated with convergent boundaries and subduction
options.B: Mid-ocean ridges and ocean trenches are the same feature

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges are elevated submarine spreading centres, not trenches. Ocean trenches are associated with convergent boundaries and subduction. These are common exam traps.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a common exam trap regarding the relationship between subduction and melting?

options.A: Subduction does not mean that the entire descending slab melts immediately; fluids released from the slab promote melting in the mantle wedge
options.B: The entire slab melts immediately upon subduction
options.C: No melting occurs above subduction zones
options.D: Melting occurs only at transform boundaries

questions.explanation: Subduction does not mean that the entire descending slab melts immediately; fluids released from the slab promote melting in the mantle wedge. This is a common exam trap.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the correct one-line description of divergent boundaries?

options.A: Plates move apart; new oceanic crust forms at spreading ridges
options.B: Plates move together; subduction or collision occurs
options.C: Plates slide past one another; earthquakes are common

questions.explanation: Divergent boundaries: plates move apart; new oceanic crust forms at spreading ridges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the correct one-line description of convergent boundaries?

options.A: Plates move apart; new oceanic crust forms at spreading ridges
options.B: Plates move together; subduction or collision occurs
options.C: Plates slide past one another; earthquakes are common

questions.explanation: Convergent boundaries: plates move together; subduction or collision occurs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the correct one-line description of transform boundaries?

options.A: Plates move apart; new oceanic crust forms at spreading ridges
options.B: Plates move together; subduction or collision occurs
options.C: Plates slide past one another; earthquakes are common

questions.explanation: Transform boundaries: plates slide past one another; earthquakes are common.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the correct one-line description of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge?

options.A: Major divergent boundary in the Atlantic Ocean
options.B: Major convergent boundary in the Pacific Ocean

questions.explanation: Mid-Atlantic Ridge: major divergent boundary in the Atlantic Ocean.
